whatIsTale.a: Tale is an open-source, self-hosted platform that orchestrates AI agents: it connects the agents and CLIs your team already uses, pools their knowledge into one governed knowledge base, and runs automations with human approval — on your own infrastructure or in a managed Swiss/EU cloud.

openSource.a: Yes. Tale is MIT-licensed and the full feature set ships in the free Community edition — Enterprise adds support and services, not features.

onPrem.q: Can Tale run fully on-premises or air-gapped?
onPrem.a: Yes. Tale self-hosts on your VPC, on-premises hardware, or fully air-gapped environments; with local models, no data ever leaves your network.

enterprisePricing.a: Enterprise is billed per user/month, with two months free when paying yearly. Storage beyond the included quota is billed per TB/month. The Community edition stays free for self-hosted use.

enterpriseFeatures.q: Are there additional features in the Enterprise plan?
enterpriseFeatures.a: No. All product features are available in the open source version too. Enterprise adds extended support and services.

byoModels.q: Do I have to bring my own AI models?
byoModels.a: No. You can bring your own models, but it's not required. We support most major AI providers and don't add fees on top — cloud AI model usage is priced at the rates of your chosen provider and is not included in the plans.

aiProviders.q: Can I use my preferred AI provider?
aiProviders.a: Yes — we support all major cloud AI providers, so you can use your preferred provider while benefiting from better pricing, higher uptime, and usage-based billing.

hardware.a: Yes — we provide hardware on rental, leasing, or purchase terms. Mention it when you contact us and we'll quote the configuration that fits.

ownHardwareModels.q: Can I use my own hardware and AI models?
ownHardwareModels.a: Yes. We're hardware- and model-agnostic, so you're free to use your own.

customTraining.q: Do you offer custom AI model training?
customTraining.a: Yes. We train and fine-tune custom models for clients. If you're interested, bring it up in the demo call.

categories.modelInfo: Suggested model for a multi-node setup. Single-node configurations can run smaller variants — your team picks the actual model at deploy time.
categories.sizeInfo: Approximate dimensions — actual size may vary slightly.
categories.ramInfo: Fast memory used for AI workloads, e.g. GDDR7 video memory or Unified Memory (UMA).
categories.umaInfo: Unified Memory Architecture — RAM shared between CPU and GPU on a single chip (Apple Silicon).
categories.gddr7Info: 7th-generation graphics DDR — high-bandwidth video memory on the GPU board, optimised for AI inference workloads.
categories.ddr5Info: Fifth-generation DDR SDRAM (faster, more efficient than DDR4).
categories.ddr5eccInfo: DDR5 with error-correcting code — server-grade memory that detects and corrects single-bit faults.
categories.int4Info: 4-bit integer quantization — trades a small amount of model precision for ~4× less memory.
categories.m2nvmeInfo: m.2 NVMe SSDs in a ZFS RAID pool — fast, redundant storage.
